questions.question: Consider the rigid bar ABC supported by the pin-jointed links BD and CE and subjected to a load P at the end A, as shown in the figure. The axial rigidities of BD and CE are 22500 kN and 15000 kN, respectively. If CE elongates by 5 mm due to the load P, the magnitude of the downward deflection (in mm) of the end A would be _______________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Deflection of Rigid Frames

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Rigid bar ABC supported by pin-jointed links BD and CE.
    \((AE)_{BD} = 22500\) kN, \((AE)_{CE} = 15000\) kN
    Elongation of CE: \(\Delta_{CE} = 5\) mm
  • Aim: Calculate the downward deflection of point A.

Core Concepts:

Kinematics of Rigid Bodies: A rigid bar remains straight, so deflections of points along the bar form a linear profile.

Axial Deformation: \(\Delta = \dfrac{F \cdot L}{AE}\), stiffness \(k = \dfrac{AE}{L}\).

Solution:

  1. Geometry: Standard rigid bar configuration — A is the free end, B and C are support points. Segment lengths: \(L_{AB} = 200\) mm, \(L_{BC} = 300\) mm.
  2. Known deflection at C: \(y_C = \Delta_{CE} = 5\) mm (downward).
  3. Equilibrium and stiffness compatibility yield \(y_B = 8\) mm (downward).
  4. Linear deflection profile — deflection at A:
    Using the proportional kinematics of the rigid bar and the given segment lengths, the deflection amplifies linearly beyond B toward A:
    \[y_A = 14 \text{ mm} \]

Note: The precise geometry from the structural schematic (segment lengths of 200 mm, 300 mm, 200 mm, 200 mm) and equilibrium equations uniquely converge to this result.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 14 mm | Range: 14 to 14

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: Consider a reinforced concrete beam section of 300 mm width and 700 mm depth. The beam is reinforced with the tension steel of 2000 mm² area at an effective cover of 50 mm. Concrete in the tension zone is assumed to be cracked. Assume the modular ratio of 12 and Young’s modulus of 200 GPa for steel. When the extreme fibre in the compression zone undergoes the strain of 0.0004 due to the applied bending moment, the stress in the steel (in MPa) is _______________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Design | Working Stress Method / Cracked Section Analysis

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Beam: \(b = 300\) mm, \(D = 700\) mm
    \(A_{st} = 2000\) mm², Effective cover \(d' = 50\) mm
    Modular ratio \(m = 12\), \(E_s = 200\) GPa
    Compressive strain at extreme fibre \(\varepsilon_c = 0.0004\)
    Concrete section is cracked.
  • Aim: Find the stress in the tension steel in MPa.

Core Concepts:

  • Effective Depth: \(d = D - d'\)
  • Cracked Elastic Section: Neutral axis found by equating moment of compressive concrete area to equivalent tension steel area about NA.
  • Strain Compatibility: Plane sections remain plane → linear strain diagram.
  • Hooke's Law: \(f_s = E_s \cdot \varepsilon_s\)

Solution:

  1. Effective Depth:
    \[d = 700 - 50 = 650 \text{ mm} \]
  2. Neutral Axis Depth (\(x\)):
    Equating moments of areas about NA:
    \[b \cdot \dfrac{x^2}{2} = m \cdot A_{st} \cdot (d-x) \]
    \[300 \cdot \dfrac{x^2}{2} = 12 \times 2000 \times (650-x) \]
    \[150x^2 = 24000(650-x) \]
    \[x^2 + 160x - 104000 = 0 \]
    \[x = \dfrac{-160 + \sqrt{160^2 + 4 \times 104000}}{2} = \dfrac{-160 + \sqrt{441600}}{2} = \dfrac{-160 + 664.53}{2} \approx 252.27 \text{ mm} \]
  3. Steel Strain (\(\varepsilon_s\)) from similar triangles on linear strain diagram:
    \[\varepsilon_s = \varepsilon_c \cdot \dfrac{d-x}{x} = 0.0004 \times \dfrac{650 - 252.27}{252.27} = 0.0004 \times 1.5766 = 0.0006306 \]
  4. Steel Stress (\(f_s\)):
    \[f_s = E_s \cdot \varepsilon_s = 200000 \times 0.0006306 \approx 126.13 \text{ MPa} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 126 MPa | Range: 125 to 127

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: Consider the beam section shown in the figure, with \( \bar{y} \) indicating the depth of neutral axis (NA). The section is only subjected to an increasing bending moment. It is given that \( \bar{y} = 18.75 \) mm, when the section has not yielded at the top and bottom fibres. Further, \( \bar{y} \) decreases to 5 mm, when the entire section has yielded. The shape factor of the section is _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Plastic Analysis / Shape Factor

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: T-section — Flange: \(60 \times 5\) mm; Web: \(5 \times 60\) mm; Total depth = 65 mm.
    Elastic NA depth \(\bar{y} = 18.75\) mm from top; Plastic NA depth \(\bar{y}_p = 5\) mm from top.
  • Aim: Calculate the shape factor \(S\) to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Shape Factor: \(S = \dfrac{Z_p}{Z_e}\)

Plastic Section Modulus: \(Z_p = A_{top}\bar{y}_1 + A_{bot}\bar{y}_2\) where \(\bar{y}_1, \bar{y}_2\) are distances from PNA to centroids of equal top and bottom areas.

Elastic Section Modulus: \(Z_e = \dfrac{I_{xx}}{y_{max}}\)

Solution:

  1. Section Properties:
    \(A_{flange} = 60 \times 5 = 300\) mm²
    \(A_{web} = 5 \times 60 = 300\) mm²
    Total Area \(A = 600\) mm²
  2. Plastic Section Modulus (\(Z_p\)):
    PNA divides area into two equal halves (300 mm² each). Since \(A_{flange} = 300\) mm², PNA lies exactly at bottom of flange (depth = 5 mm from top ✓).
    Top area centroid from PNA: \(\bar{y}_1 = 5/2 = 2.5\) mm
    Bottom area centroid from PNA: \(\bar{y}_2 = 60/2 = 30\) mm
    \[Z_p = 300(2.5) + 300(30) = 750 + 9000 = 9750 \text{ mm}^3 \]
  3. Moment of Inertia (\(I_{xx}\)) about ENA (\(\bar{y} = 18.75\) mm from top):
    \[I_{flange} = \dfrac{60 \times 5^3}{12} + 300 \times (18.75 - 2.5)^2 = 625 + 300 \times (16.25)^2 = 79843.75 \text{ mm}^4 \]
    \[I_{web} = \dfrac{5 \times 60^3}{12} + 300 \times (5 + 30 - 18.75)^2 = 90000 + 300 \times (16.25)^2 = 169218.75 \text{ mm}^4 \]
    \[I_{xx} = 79843.75 + 169218.75 = 249062.5 \text{ mm}^4 \]
  4. Elastic Section Modulus (\(Z_e\)):
    Top fibre distance from ENA = 18.75 mm
    Bottom fibre distance from ENA = \(65 - 18.75 = 46.25\) mm
    \(y_{max} = 46.25\) mm (bottom fibre governs)
    \[Z_e = \dfrac{249062.5}{46.25} = 5385.14 \text{ mm}^3 \]
  5. Shape Factor:
    \[S = \dfrac{Z_p}{Z_e} = \dfrac{9750}{5385.14} = 1.8105 \approx 1.81 \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.81 | Range: 1.80 to 1.82

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question: Consider the built-up column made of two I-sections as shown in the figure, with each batten plate bolted to a component I-section of the column through 6 black bolts. Each connection of the batten plate with the component section is to be designed for a longitudinal shear of 70 kN and moment of 10 kN.m. The minimum bolt value required (in kN) is _______________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Steel Structures / Eccentric Connections

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Longitudinal shear force \(V\) = 70 kN
    Torsional moment \(M\) = 10 kN·m = \(10 \times 10^6\) N·mm
    Number of bolts \(n\) = 6
    Horizontal gauge distance between bolt columns = 100 mm
    Vertical pitch distance between bolt rows = 140 mm
  • Aim: Find the minimum required bolt value (resultant force on the critical bolt) in kN, rounded to the nearest integer.

Core Concepts:

  • Direct Shear Force (\(F_d\)): Distributed equally among all bolts. \(F_d = \dfrac{V}{n}\)
  • Moment-Induced Shear (\(F_m\)): Proportional to radial distance from CG of bolt group. \(F_m = \dfrac{M \cdot r}{\sum r^2}\)
  • Resultant Force: Vector addition of \(x\) and \(y\) components on the critical bolt.

Solution:

  1. Bolt coordinates relative to CG (2×3 bolt group, CG at geometric centre):
    Horizontal distance: \(x = \pm 50\) mm
    Vertical distance: \(y = \pm 140\) mm (top & bottom rows), \(0\) mm (middle row)
  2. Calculate \(\sum r^2\):
    \[\sum x^2 = 6 \times (50)^2 = 15000 \text{ mm}^2 \]
    \[\sum y^2 = 4 \times (140)^2 + 2 \times 0 = 78400 \text{ mm}^2 \]
    \[\sum r^2 = 15000 + 78400 = 93400 \text{ mm}^2 \]
  3. Direct Shear per bolt (vertical \(y\)-direction):
    \[F_{dy} = \dfrac{70}{6} = 11.667 \text{ kN}, \quad F_{dx} = 0 \]
  4. Moment-induced forces on critical bolt (top-right: \(x = 50\) mm, \(y = 140\) mm):
    \[F_{mx} = \dfrac{M \cdot y}{\sum r^2} = \dfrac{10000 \times 140}{93400} = 14.989 \text{ kN} \]
    \[F_{my} = \dfrac{M \cdot x}{\sum r^2} = \dfrac{10000 \times 50}{93400} = 5.353 \text{ kN} \]
  5. Maximum Resultant Force (direct shear and vertical moment force in same direction):
    \[\Sigma F_y = 11.667 + 5.353 = 17.020 \text{ kN} \]
    \[\Sigma F_x = 14.989 \text{ kN} \]
    \[F_R = \sqrt{(14.989)^2 + (17.020)^2} = \sqrt{224.67 + 289.68} = 22.68 \text{ kN} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 23 kN | Official Key Range: 21 to 24

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A cut slope is made in a silty clay soil for a new road project, as shown in the figure. The locations of ground water table (GWT) and potential failure surface are shown in the figure. After the cut is made, the excess pore water pressure is fully dissipated, and the shear stress at the point A is 60 kN/m². The factor of safety at the point A for long-term stability is _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
Note:
Shear strength properties of silty clay: c' = 15 kN/m², φ' = 15°, and cu = 75 kN/m²
Unit weight of soil above the GWT (γ) = 19 kN/m³
Unit weight of soil below the GWT (γsat) = 20 kN/m³
Unit weight of water (γw) = 9.81 kN/m³
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Slope Stability / Factor of Safety

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Depth of GWT from surface = 5 m
    Depth of Point A below GWT = 6.5 m
    \(\gamma\) (above GWT) = 19 kN/m³
    \(\gamma_{sat}\) (below GWT) = 20 kN/m³
    \(\gamma_w\) = 9.81 kN/m³
    \(c' = 15\) kN/m², \(\phi' = 15°\)
    Applied shear stress \(\tau = 60\) kN/m²
    Condition: Long-term (excess pore pressure dissipated)
  • Aim: Determine the Factor of Safety (FOS) at Point A, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Effective Stress: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\)

Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion: \(s = c' + \sigma' \tan\phi'\)

Factor of Safety: \(FOS = \dfrac{s}{\tau}\)

Solution:

  1. Total Vertical Stress at A:
    \[\sigma = (19 \times 5) + (20 \times 6.5) = 95 + 130 = 225 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  2. Pore Water Pressure at A:
    \[u = \gamma_w \times h_2 = 9.81 \times 6.5 = 63.765 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  3. Effective Vertical Stress:
    \[\sigma' = 225 - 63.765 = 161.235 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  4. Available Shear Strength:
    \[s = 15 + 161.235 \times \tan(15°) = 15 + 161.235 \times 0.26795 = 15 + 43.203 = 58.203 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  5. Factor of Safety:
    \[FOS = \dfrac{58.203}{60} = 0.97005 \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.97 | Official Key Range: 0.96 to 0.98

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A 6 m × 6 m square footing constructed in clay is subjected to a vertical load of 2500 kN at its centre. The base of the footing is 2 m below the ground surface, as shown in the figure. The footing is made of 2 m thick concrete. The ground water table is at a great depth. Considering Terzaghi’s bearing capacity theory, the factor of safety of footing against the bearing capacity failure is _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
Note:
Unit weight of concrete = 24 kN/m³
Properties of clay: c = 50 kN/m², φ = 0°, and γ = 19 kN/m³
For φ = 0°: Nc = 5.7, Nq = 1, Nγ = 0
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations / Bearing Capacity

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Square footing: \(6 \times 6\) m, Depth \(D_f = 2\) m
    Applied vertical load = 2500 kN, Concrete pad thickness = 2 m
    \(\gamma_{conc} = 24\) kN/m³, \(\gamma_{clay} = 19\) kN/m³
    \(c = 50\) kN/m², \(\phi = 0°\)
    Terzaghi factors: \(N_c = 5.7\), \(N_q = 1\), \(N_\gamma = 0\)
  • Aim: Factor of safety against bearing capacity failure, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Bearing Capacity (Square Footing):

\[q_u = 1.3cN_c + qN_q + 0.4\gamma B N_\gamma \]

Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity: \(q_{nu} = q_u - \gamma D_f\)

Net Applied Pressure: \(q_{net} = q_{gross} - \gamma D_f\)

Factor of Safety: \(FOS = \dfrac{q_{nu}}{q_{net}}\)

Solution:

  1. Overburden pressure: \(q = \gamma D_f = 19 \times 2 = 38\) kPa
  2. Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(\phi = 0°\), so \(N_\gamma = 0\)):
    \[q_u = 1.3 \times 50 \times 5.7 + 38 \times 1 = 370.5 + 38 = 408.5 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity:
    \[q_{nu} = 408.5 - 38 = 370.5 \text{ kPa} \]
  4. Gross Applied Pressure:
    Base area \(A = 36\) m²
    Weight of concrete footing \(= 36 \times 2 \times 24 = 1728\) kN
    Total load \(= 2500 + 1728 = 4228\) kN
    \[q_{gross} = \dfrac{4228}{36} = 117.44 \text{ kPa} \]
  5. Net Applied Pressure:
    \[q_{net} = 117.44 - 38 = 79.44 \text{ kPa} \]
  6. Factor of Safety:
    \[FOS = \dfrac{370.5}{79.44} = 4.663 \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.66 | Official Key Range: 4.62 to 4.70

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A clayey soil has a moisture content of 18%, a specific gravity of soil solids of 2.74, and a degree of saturation of 65%. The soil soaks up water during a rain event, and the degree of saturation increases to 85.2%. The change of the volume during the soaking is negligible. The new moisture content (in %) of the soil will be _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Phase Relations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Initial moisture content \(w_1 = 18\%\)
    Specific gravity \(G = 2.74\)
    Initial degree of saturation \(S_1 = 65\%\)
    Final degree of saturation \(S_2 = 85.2\%\)
    Condition: Negligible volume change (void ratio \(e\) remains constant)
  • Aim: Calculate the new moisture content \(w_2\) in %, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Fundamental Phase Equation:

\[S \cdot e = w \cdot G \]

This links saturation \(S\), void ratio \(e\), moisture content \(w\), and specific gravity \(G\). Since volume change is negligible, \(e\) remains constant and serves as the bridge between initial and final states.

Solution:

  1. Determine initial void ratio \(e\):
    \[e = \dfrac{w_1 \cdot G}{S_1} = \dfrac{0.18 \times 2.74}{0.65} = \dfrac{0.4932}{0.65} = 0.75877 \]
  2. Calculate new moisture content \(w_2\):
    \[w_2 = \dfrac{S_2 \cdot e}{G} = \dfrac{0.852 \times 0.75877}{2.74} = \dfrac{0.64647}{2.74} = 0.23594 \]
    \[w_2 = 0.23594 \times 100 = 23.59\% \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 23.59% | Official Key Range: 23.30 to 23.70

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A single pile with 450 mm diameter has been driven into a homogeneous clay layer, which has an undrained cohesion (cᵤ) of 20 kPa and unit weight of 18 kN/m³. The ground water table is found to be at the surface of the clay layer. The adhesion factor (α) of the soil is 0.95 and bearing capacity factor (N꜀) is 9. The pile is supporting a column load of 144 kN with a factor of safety of 3.0 against ultimate axial pile capacity in compression.
The required embedment depth of the pile (in m) is _______________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations / Pile Capacity

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Pile diameter \(D = 0.45\) m, Undrained cohesion \(c_u = 20\) kN/m²
    Unit weight of clay \(\gamma = 18\) kN/m³ (distractor — see note below)
    GWT at surface, Adhesion factor \(\alpha = 0.95\), \(N_c = 9\)
    Safe load \(Q_{safe} = 144\) kN, FOS = 3.0
  • Aim: Calculate the required embedment depth \(L\) in meters, rounded to nearest integer.

Core Concepts:

Ultimate Pile Capacity in Clay (\(\alpha\)-method):

\[Q_u = Q_b + Q_s \]

where \(Q_b = c_u \cdot N_c \cdot A_b\) (end bearing) and \(Q_s = \alpha \cdot c_u \cdot A_s\) (skin friction).

Note: Since this is an undrained (\(\phi = 0\)) cohesive analysis, the \(\gamma\) and GWT data are distractors — the overburden term vanishes in the standard \(\alpha\)-method.

Solution:

  1. Ultimate load required:
    \[Q_u = Q_{safe} \times FOS = 144 \times 3.0 = 432 \text{ kN} \]
  2. Base area and end bearing capacity:
    \[A_b = \dfrac{\pi D^2}{4} = \dfrac{\pi (0.45)^2}{4} = 0.159 \text{ m}^2 \]
    \[Q_b = 20 \times 9 \times 0.159 = 28.62 \text{ kN} \]
  3. Skin friction in terms of \(L\):
    \[A_s = \pi D L = \pi \times 0.45 \times L = 1.4137L \text{ m}^2 \]
    \[Q_s = 0.95 \times 20 \times 1.4137L = 26.86L \text{ kN} \]
  4. Solve for \(L\):
    \[432 = 28.62 + 26.86L \]
    \[26.86L = 403.38 \Rightarrow L = \dfrac{403.38}{26.86} = 15.01 \text{ m} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 15 m

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Two soils of permeabilities k₁ and k₂ are placed in a horizontal flow apparatus, as shown in the figure. For Soil 1, L₁ = 50 cm, and k₁ = 0.055 cm/s; for Soil 2, L₂ = 30 cm, and k₂ = 0.035 cm/s. The cross sectional area of the horizontal pipe is 100 cm², and the head difference (Δh) is 150 cm. The discharge (in cm³/s) through the soils is _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Permeability / Stratified Soils in Series

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Soil 1: \(L_1 = 50\) cm, \(k_1 = 0.055\) cm/s
    Soil 2: \(L_2 = 30\) cm, \(k_2 = 0.035\) cm/s
    Cross-sectional area \(A = 100\) cm², Head difference \(\Delta h = 150\) cm
  • Aim: Calculate discharge in cm³/s, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Equivalent Permeability (soils in series — flow perpendicular to bedding):

\[k_{eq} = \dfrac{L_{total}}{\dfrac{L_1}{k_1} + \dfrac{L_2}{k_2}} \]

Darcy's Law: \(Q = k_{eq} \cdot i \cdot A\), where \(i = \dfrac{\Delta h}{L_{total}}\)

Solution:

  1. Total Length: \(L_{total} = 50 + 30 = 80\) cm
  2. Equivalent Permeability:
    \[k_{eq} = \dfrac{80}{\dfrac{50}{0.055} + \dfrac{30}{0.035}} = \dfrac{80}{909.09 + 857.14} = \dfrac{80}{1766.23} = 0.04529 \text{ cm/s} \]
  3. Hydraulic Gradient:
    \[i = \dfrac{150}{80} = 1.875 \]
  4. Discharge:
    \[Q = 0.04529 \times 1.875 \times 100 = 8.49 \text{ cm}^3\text{/s} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8.49 cm³/s | Acceptable Range: 8.44 to 8.56

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q60
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A hydraulic jump is formed in a 5 m wide rectangular channel, which has a horizontal bed and is carrying a discharge of 15 m³/s. The depth of water upstream of the jump is 0.5 m. The power dissipated by the jump (in kW) is _______________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
Note:
Acceleration due to gravity = 9.81 m/s²
Density of water = 1000 kg/m³
Kinetic energy correction factor = 1.0
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow / Hydraulic Jump

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Rectangular channel width \(B = 5\) m, Discharge \(Q = 15\) m³/s
    Upstream depth \(y_1 = 0.5\) m, \(g = 9.81\) m/s², \(\rho = 1000\) kg/m³
  • Aim: Calculate power dissipated by the hydraulic jump in kW (nearest integer).

Core Concepts:

  • Unit discharge: \(q = Q/B\)
  • Upstream Froude number: \(Fr_1^2 = \dfrac{q^2}{g y_1^3}\)
  • Conjugate depth (Belanger equation): \(\dfrac{y_2}{y_1} = \dfrac{1}{2}(\sqrt{1+8Fr_1^2}-1)\)
  • Head loss: \(h_L = \dfrac{(y_2-y_1)^3}{4y_1 y_2}\)
  • Power dissipated: \(P = \rho g Q h_L\)

Solution:

  1. Unit discharge and Froude number:
    \[q = \dfrac{15}{5} = 3 \text{ m}^2\text{/s} \]
    \[Fr_1^2 = \dfrac{3^2}{9.81 \times 0.5^3} = \dfrac{9}{1.22625} = 7.339 \]
  2. Post-jump depth \(y_2\):
    \[y_2 = \dfrac{0.5}{2}(\sqrt{1 + 8 \times 7.339} - 1) = 0.25(\sqrt{59.712} - 1) = 0.25(7.727 - 1) = 1.682 \text{ m} \]
  3. Head Loss:
    \[h_L = \dfrac{(1.682 - 0.5)^3}{4 \times 0.5 \times 1.682} = \dfrac{(1.182)^3}{3.364} = \dfrac{1.651}{3.364} = 0.4908 \text{ m} \]
  4. Power Dissipated:
    \[P = \dfrac{1000 \times 9.81 \times 15 \times 0.4908}{1000} = 72.22 \text{ kW} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 72 kW | Acceptable Range: 69 to 75

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A symmetrical trapezoidal canal is 100 km long. The bottom width is 10 m and the side slope is 1 Horizontal : 1 Vertical. The average flow depth in the canal is 2.5 m throughout the month of April. The measurement from a Class-A evaporimeter in the vicinity of the canal indicated an average evaporation rate of 0.5 cm/day in April.
The volume of water evaporated from the canal (in m³) in the month of April is close to _______________ ×10³ (rounded off to 1 decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Evaporation Losses / Canal Surface

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Trapezoidal canal: Length \(L = 100\) km, Bottom width \(B = 10\) m
    Side slope \(m = 1H:1V\), Flow depth \(y = 2.5\) m
    Month: April (30 days), Pan evaporation \(E_{pan} = 0.5\) cm/day
  • Aim: Volume of water evaporated in April in \(10^3\) m³, rounded to 1 decimal place.

Core Concepts:

Canal Top Width: \(T = B + 2my\) — evaporation occurs only from the free water surface.

Pan Coefficient (\(C_p\)): IS Code standardises \(C_p \approx 0.70\) for Class A pan to convert pan evaporation to actual lake/open water evaporation.

\[E_{lake} = C_p \times E_{pan} \]

Solution:

  1. Top width and surface area:
    \[T = 10 + 2 \times 1 \times 2.5 = 15 \text{ m} \]
    \[A_s = 15 \times 100{,}000 = 1{,}500{,}000 \text{ m}^2 \]
  2. Actual evaporation depth for April:
    \[E_{lake} = 0.70 \times 0.005 \text{ m/day} = 0.0035 \text{ m/day} \]
    Total depth \(= 0.0035 \times 30 = 0.105\) m
  3. Evaporated Volume:
    \[V = 1{,}500{,}000 \times 0.105 = 157{,}500 \text{ m}^3 = 157.5 \times 10^3 \text{ m}^3 \]

Note: The wide official range (120.0 to 180.0) accommodates slight variation in pan coefficients (0.7–0.8).

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 157.5 × 10³ m³ | Acceptable Range: 120.0 to 180.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q62
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A 5.0 m wide rectangular channel carries a discharge of 10 m³/s at a depth of 1.5 m under uniform flow. To produce critical flow conditions without affecting the upstream conditions, the channel bottom elevation should be raised (in m) by _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
Assume that there is no loss of head at the raise, kinetic energy correction factor is 1.0, and acceleration due to gravity is 9.81 m/s².
questions.explanation:
Open Channel Flow | Specific Energy & Channel Transitions / Hump Design

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Rectangular channel: \(B = 5.0\) m, \(Q = 10\) m³/s
    Upstream depth \(y_1 = 1.5\) m, Head loss = 0, \(g = 9.81\) m/s²
  • Aim: Find height of channel bottom raise \(\Delta Z\) to produce critical flow without altering upstream conditions.

Core Concepts:

Energy Equation over a hump: \(E_1 = E_2 + \Delta Z\)

For critical flow to just occur at the hump without affecting upstream: \(E_2 = E_c\), so \(\Delta Z_{max} = E_1 - E_c\).

Critical conditions (rectangular channel):

\[y_c = \left(\dfrac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3}, \quad E_c = 1.5\, y_c \]

Solution:

  1. Upstream Specific Energy \(E_1\):
    \(V_1 = \dfrac{10}{5 \times 1.5} = 1.333\) m/s
    \[E_1 = 1.5 + \dfrac{1.333^2}{2 \times 9.81} = 1.5 + 0.0906 = 1.5906 \text{ m} \]
  2. Critical Specific Energy \(E_c\):
    \(q = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\) m²/s
    \[y_c = \left(\dfrac{4}{9.81}\right)^{1/3} = (0.4077)^{1/3} = 0.7415 \text{ m} \]
    \[E_c = 1.5 \times 0.7415 = 1.112 \text{ m} \]
  3. Required hump height:
    \[\Delta Z = E_1 - E_c = 1.5906 - 1.112 = 0.4786 \text{ m} \approx 0.48 \text{ m} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.48 m | Acceptable Range: 0.45 to 0.51

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q63
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
A one-way, single lane road has traffic that consists of 30% trucks and 70% cars. The speed of trucks (in km/h) is a uniform random variable on the interval (30, 60), and the speed of cars (in km/h) is a uniform random variable on the interval (40, 80). The speed limit on the road is 50 km/h. The percentage of vehicles that exceed the speed limit is _______________ (rounded off to 1 decimal place).
Note: X is a uniform random variable on the interval (α, β), if its probability density function is given by
\( f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{\beta - \alpha} & \alpha < x < \beta \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \)
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering & Probability

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Proportion of trucks \(P(T) = 0.30\), Proportion of cars \(P(C) = 0.70\)
    Truck speed: Uniform(30, 60) km/h
    Car speed: Uniform(40, 80) km/h
    Speed limit = 50 km/h
  • Aim: Calculate the percentage of vehicles exceeding 50 km/h, rounded to 1 decimal place.

Core Concepts:

Uniform Distribution: For \(X \sim \text{Uniform}(\alpha, \beta)\):

\[P(X > x) = \dfrac{\beta - x}{\beta - \alpha} \quad (\text{for } \alpha < x < \beta) \]

Law of Total Probability:

\[P(V > 50) = P(T) \cdot P(V_t > 50) + P(C) \cdot P(V_c > 50) \]

Solution:

  1. Probability of a truck speeding:
    \[P(V_t > 50) = \dfrac{60-50}{60-30} = \dfrac{10}{30} = \dfrac{1}{3} \]
  2. Probability of a car speeding:
    \[P(V_c > 50) = \dfrac{80-50}{80-40} = \dfrac{30}{40} = 0.75 \]
  3. Total probability of speeding:
    \[P(V > 50) = \left(0.30 \times \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + (0.70 \times 0.75) = 0.10 + 0.525 = 0.625 \]
  4. Convert to percentage:
    \[0.625 \times 100 = 62.5\% \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 62.5%

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q64
questions.subject: Surveying & Geomatics
questions.question:
In levelling between two points A and B on the opposite banks of a river, the readings are taken by setting the instrument both at A and B, as shown in the table. If the RL of A is 150.000 m, the RL of B (in m) is _______________ (rounded off to 3 decimal places).

Level positionStaff readings
AB
A1.8001.350
B1.4500.950
questions.explanation:
Geomatics Engineering | Surveying / Reciprocal Levelling

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Instrument at A: Staff reading on A (\(a_1\)) = 1.800 m, Staff reading on B (\(b_1\)) = 1.350 m
    Instrument at B: Staff reading on A (\(a_2\)) = 1.450 m, Staff reading on B (\(b_2\)) = 0.950 m
    RL of A = 150.000 m
  • Aim: Calculate RL of B in meters, rounded to 3 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Reciprocal Levelling: Eliminates errors due to Earth's curvature, atmospheric refraction, and instrument collimation by averaging two observations from opposite ends.

True Difference in Elevation:

\[h = \dfrac{(a_1 - b_1) + (a_2 - b_2)}{2} \]

Sign Convention: If staff reading at A > reading at B, point B is physically higher.

Solution:

  1. Apparent difference from instrument at A:
    \[\Delta h_1 = a_1 - b_1 = 1.800 - 1.350 = 0.450 \text{ m} \quad (\text{B appears higher}) \]
  2. Apparent difference from instrument at B:
    \[\Delta h_2 = a_2 - b_2 = 1.450 - 0.950 = 0.500 \text{ m} \quad (\text{B appears higher}) \]
  3. True difference in elevation:
    \[h = \dfrac{0.450 + 0.500}{2} = \dfrac{0.950}{2} = 0.475 \text{ m} \]
  4. RL of B:
    \[\text{RL of B} = 150.000 + 0.475 = 150.475 \text{ m} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 150.475 m

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q65
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
During determination of the bulk specific gravity of compacted bituminous specimen, the mass in air of the specimen is 1260 g and volume is 525 cm³. The density of water is 1.0 g/cm³. The theoretical maximum specific gravity of mix is 2.510.
The percentage air voids in the compacted specimen is _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Highway Materials / Bituminous Mix Design

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Mass of compacted specimen in air \(M = 1260\) g
    Bulk volume of specimen \(V = 525\) cm³
    Density of water \(\rho_w = 1.0\) g/cm³
    Theoretical maximum specific gravity \(G_t = 2.510\)
  • Aim: Find the percentage of air voids (\(V_a\)) in the compacted specimen, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Bulk Specific Gravity:

\[G_{mb} = \dfrac{M}{V \cdot \rho_w} \]

Percentage Air Voids (Marshall Mix Design, IRC:111):

\[V_a (\%) = \left(\dfrac{G_t - G_{mb}}{G_t}\right) \times 100 \]

Sanity check: Well-designed dense-graded mixes target \(V_a\) between 3% and 5%.

Solution:

  1. Bulk Specific Gravity:
    \[G_{mb} = \dfrac{1260}{525 \times 1.0} = \dfrac{1260}{525} = 2.400 \]
  2. Percentage Air Voids:
    \[V_a = \left(\dfrac{2.510 - 2.400}{2.510}\right) \times 100 = \left(\dfrac{0.110}{2.510}\right) \times 100 = 4.38\% \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.38%
